rules.title: Rent control and vacancy decontrol limits
rules.requirement: Landlords may not charge rent above the amount authorized by Chapter 155, and capital-improvement or hardship increases require Rent Leveling and Stabilization Board approval. Vacancy decontrol is limited for ordinary vacancies, while qualifying bona fide condo/co-op owner-occupant units may set an initial post-occupancy rent but are otherwise subject to Chapter 155.
rules.key_value: Capital improvement surcharge may not increase base rent by more than 33 1/3% in any one twelve-month period; ordinary vacancy decontrol initial rent is limited to 25% over the last rental paid and no dwelling unit may be decontrolled more than once in any three-year period.

coverage.summary: Applies to Hoboken dwellings subject to Chapter 155, including registered rent-controlled properties and specified vacancy-decontrol situations.

rules.exemptions: Upon a qualifying voluntary vacancy or legal eviction, a registered apartment unit is decontrolled only for the new tenant's initial rental, subject to the 25% cap, and then later increases are subject to Chapter 155. A bona fide condo/co-op owner-occupant who has continuously occupied the unit as a principal residence for the previous two years may establish the initial rent after vacating, but the unit otherwise remains subject to Chapter 155.
rules.penalty: A violation of Chapter 155 is punishable under N.J.S.A. 40:49-5, including a fine not exceeding $2,000; each dwelling unit and each unlawful demand or payment is a separate violation, with additional repeat-offender fines possible.
rules.interaction: The ordinance states that additional rental increases beyond an initial vacancy-decontrol rent are subject to Chapter 155 and that capital-improvement and hardship increases require Board approval under the chapter.

rules.law_name: Temporary Moratorium on Rent Increases During COVID-19 Pandemic State of Emergency
rules.effective_date_basis: The moratorium shall be made retroactive to April 1, 2020, and shall remain in effect until May 7, 2022.
rules.title: COVID-19 rent-increase moratorium
rules.requirement: During the moratorium, landlords could not increase rent or additional charges for tenants covered by Chapter 155. After the moratorium, permitted increases could be applied prospectively at a new tenancy or lease renewal, but landlords could not demand retroactive payments and no 2020 CPI increase was allowed for the moratorium period.
rules.key_value: No rent increases from 2020-04-01 through 2022-05-07; no retroactive payment; no CPI increase for April 1, 2020 through the end of 2020.

rules.title: COVID-19 moratorium on increasing security deposits and related charges
rules.requirement: During the COVID-19 moratorium, landlords of properties covered by Chapter 155 could not increase security deposits, damage deposits, cleaning deposits, or other rental-associated charges. The restriction ran retroactively from April 1, 2020 through May 7, 2022.
rules.key_value: No increase in security, damage, or cleaning deposits from 2020-04-01 through 2022-05-07.
